claim: Abstract: networks of conditional independence relationships 'varied between dog types'
design: cross-sectional survey; 116 patrol vs 54 detection dogs, 20 ordinal descriptors, 2 separate GGMs
test_used: none (visual contrast of two separately fitted networks)
test_indicated: permutation test of between-group difference, handler-level label shuffle
recomputed_p: 0.666 (omnibus structure); 0.168 (mean |r|); 0/190 pairs after BH or max-stat FWER
effect: SS of polychoric differences 8.41 vs permutation median 9.21; mean |r| +0.090 (detection − patrol), null SD 0.063

claim: Abstract: 'Bootstrap analyses revealed the stability of network results'
design: resampling of dogs within each network
test_used: non-parametric bootstrap (nBoot=2000), node-wise and subject-wise bootstrap; no formal criterion
test_indicated: edge-inclusion and centrality stability at the sampled unit, reported per network
effect: patrol: 48/55 published edges present in >=50% of 80% subsamples (median inclusion 0.95); detection: 0/70 (median 0.08), 907/1000 subsamples return an empty network

claim: Abstract: 'The most central descriptors denoted desirable characteristics in both patrol and detection dog networks'
design: 20 nodes (14 desirable, 6 undesirable) within each fitted network
test_used: none (descriptive)
test_indicated: none available: nodes of one network are not independent units
effect: probability of superiority (desirable > undesirable): patrol 0.84 betweenness / 0.89 strength; detection 0.63 / 0.80

claim: Abstract: 'Playful' is widely correlated and holds mediating relationships across both networks
design: centrality of one node in two fitted networks
test_used: none (rank of point estimate)
test_indicated: rank-order stability under resampling (the authors supply this in fig. S1-S2)
effect: patrol betweenness 106 (highest of 20), strength 1.075 (2nd); detection betweenness 100 and strength 1.321 (both highest)

claim: Patrol network had 55 edges (28.95% of possible); detection network had 70 edges (36.84%)
design: EBICglasso on polychoric correlations, n=116 and n=54, gamma=0.65
test_used: none (model selection output)
test_indicated: none for the counts; densities from different n are not comparable
effect: reproduced exactly: 55 and 70 edges, edge sets identical at 190/190 pairs, max |weight difference| 0.0060 (patrol) and 0.0000 (detection)

claim: Named 'strong/salient' partial correlations in the patrol network (CUR-PLA, CUR-PS, CUR-FL, SOC-REC-WIL, GWL-FDA, SLP-FIT, ACT-FIT, FL-ADP; negative FL-STR, FoH-SLP, DA-WIL, FDA-PLA, GUS-FSH, GUS-WIL)
design: edge weights of one fitted GGM, n=116
test_used: none (lasso selection, no uncertainty reported)
test_indicated: edge-inclusion proportion under resampling
effect: all named edges reproduce; median inclusion of published patrol edges 0.95 across 1000 80% subsamples vs 0.08 for absent pairs

claim: Named 'strong/salient' partial correlations in the detection network (PLA-CUR/PSV/ADP/PS, FSH-SOC/WIL/ADP/TOY/ACT, FL-CUR, FL-PS, SLP-PS, SLP-ADP, PSV-FIT, WIL-SOC, GUS-FDA, GWL-FDA, GWL-DA; negative PLA-GUS, CUR-STR)
design: edge weights of one fitted GGM, n=54
test_used: none (lasso selection, no uncertainty reported)
test_indicated: edge-inclusion proportion under resampling
effect: all named edges reproduce from the deposited matrix, but 0/70 appear in >=50% of 80% subsamples (median inclusion 0.08); 907/1000 subsamples return an empty network

claim: 'Most of the desirable descriptors had higher observed centrality values compared with undesirable descriptors'
design: 14 vs 6 nodes within each network
test_used: none (descriptive)
test_indicated: none available (nodes are not independent units)
effect: probability of superiority 0.84/0.89 (patrol betweenness/strength), 0.63/0.80 (detection)

claim: ACT, CUR, FIT, REC and SLP had higher betweenness and strength in the patrol than the detection network
design: point-estimate comparison of two networks fitted at different n
test_used: none
test_indicated: none for a descriptive statement; a test is required for the inference drawn from it (see C11)
effect: exactly these 5 of 20 descriptors are higher on both metrics; reproduced from table S4

claim: DA, FSH, GUS, GWL, PS, PSV, STR and TOY had higher betweenness and strength in the detection than the patrol network
design: point-estimate comparison of two networks fitted at different n
test_used: none
test_indicated: none for a descriptive statement; a test is required for the inference drawn from it (see C12)
effect: exactly these 8 of 20 descriptors are higher on both metrics; reproduced from table S4

claim: Mean centrality differences in CUR (d=0.452), SLP (0.290) and ACT (0.282) 'had the largest effect sizes in favour of the patrol dog network'
design: Cliff's delta between the 2000 patrol and 2000 detection bootstrap replicate centralities
test_used: Cliff's delta with 95% CI computed on nBoot x nBoot replicates
test_indicated: permutation test against a null of exchangeable dog-type labels, with multiplicity over 20 nodes x 2 metrics
reported_p: none (CI used as the inferential device)
recomputed_p: 0.666 omnibus; 0.168 for overall association strength; 0/190 descriptor pairs survive BH (min q=0.475) or max-statistic FWER (min p=0.692)
effect: published CI half-width 0.0350 = 1.60/sqrt(nBoot): Monte-Carlo error, not sampling uncertainty; 18/20 intervals exclude 0, including 9 of the 11 the paper calls negligible

claim: FSH (d=-0.614), DA (-0.609), GUS (-0.582), TOY (-0.465), GWL (-0.310) and FDA (-0.302) 'had the largest effect sizes in favour of the detection dog network'
design: Cliff's delta between the 2000 patrol and 2000 detection bootstrap replicate centralities
test_used: Cliff's delta with 95% CI computed on nBoot x nBoot replicates
test_indicated: permutation test against a null of exchangeable dog-type labels, with multiplicity over 20 nodes x 2 metrics
reported_p: none (CI used as the inferential device)
recomputed_p: 0.666 omnibus; 0.168 for overall association strength; 0/190 descriptor pairs survive BH or max-statistic FWER
effect: same interval defect as C11; all six deltas are computed on a detection network that does not survive an 80% subsample

claim: SD of the number of edges across bootstrap samples was 12.82 (patrol) and 29.75 (detection)
design: 2000 with-replacement bootstraps per network
test_used: descriptive SD of a bootstrap distribution
test_indicated: same
effect: under qgraph 1.10.1 the same code gives mean 149.6 edges (SD 41.2) patrol and 147.1 (SD 16.3) detection; 25/25 tested resamples produced a non-positive-definite polychoric matrix and EBIC selected the minimum lambda (near-complete graph) in about two thirds of them

claim: 'Node-wise bootstrapping demonstrated reasonable stability of the original network structures ... even for networks of only three nodes'
design: resampling of nodes, not of dogs
test_used: correlation of bootstrapped with original centralities
test_indicated: resampling of the sampled unit (dogs/handlers); node-wise resampling cannot address sampling error
effect: node-wise resampling holds the 170 dogs fixed, so it is not informative about sampling variability; the authors' own subject-wise analysis and the present subsampling show the detection network is unstable

claim: Subject-wise bootstrapping: patrol networks of <=~60 dogs and detection networks of <~40 dogs correlate poorly with the original networks
design: subject-wise resampling
test_used: correlation of subsampled with original centralities
test_indicated: same
effect: corroborated: in 1000 subsamples of 43 detection dogs (80%), 907 returned an empty network; at matched n=54, patrol dogs returned an empty network in 924/1000 draws

claim: CUR and SOC share positive pairwise correlations (0.41, 0.40) but are not directly related in either network, 'suggesting that their pairwise correlation was due to common mediating variables'
design: absence of an L1-shrunk edge in two GGMs
test_used: none (a zero in a lasso solution)
test_indicated: a test of conditional independence, or an edge-inclusion proportion, before a mediation reading
effect: polychoric r reproduces at 0.414 and 0.397; the CUR-SOC edge is non-zero in 3.5% of patrol subsamples (absence is stable) but only 0.9% of detection subsamples, where 91% of subsamples are empty and absence is therefore uninformative

claim: In the detection network, aggression descriptors were 'more frequently and strongly negatively correlated with desirable descriptors ... compared to the patrol dog network'
design: counts and sums of edge weights between 3 aggression and 14 desirable descriptors
test_used: none
test_indicated: permutation test of the between-network difference in these specific edges
recomputed_p: 0/190 descriptor pairs differ between dog types after BH or max-statistic FWER
effect: detection has 4 negative aggression-desirable edges (sum -0.213) vs patrol 7 (sum -0.315), and 5 positive ones (sum +0.350) where patrol has none; the 'positively correlated with undesirable' half holds (sum +0.377 vs +0.044 outside the aggression trio)

claim: Eight descriptors were removed because repeated responses by the same handler 'lacked independence'; the remaining 20 are treated as independent observations
design: 44 handlers with repeated surveys; ordinal mixed model vs fixed-effects model
test_used: likelihood ratio test of a variance component referred to chi-square with 1 df, uncorrected across 29 descriptors
test_indicated: LRT referred to the boundary null 0.5*chi2_0 + 0.5*chi2_1
recomputed_p: FDA 0.026; GWL 0.048 (both would be removed); 8 removals become 10
effect: handler ICC in the 20 retained descriptors: median 0.114, max 0.228 (FDA), 12/20 above 0.10; mean 1.453 dogs per handler gives a design effect of 1.048, so n_eff = 162 of 170 (patrol 111, detection 52)

claim: Fifteen multiply imputed datasets were averaged and rounded to a single dataset of ordinal responses, which was then analysed
design: 1.2 +/- 1.03% missing responses across 29 descriptors
test_used: mean of 15 imputations, rounded to integers
test_indicated: analyse each imputation and pool by Rubin's rules, or use one imputation and say so
effect: averaging across imputations discards the between-imputation variance that is the purpose of multiple imputation and treats imputed values as observed; with ~1.2% missing the magnitude is small and no claim here turns on it

claim: gamma = 0.65 was chosen as 'the most conservative value ... where values above this resulted in empty graphs for the detection dog network'
design: tuning of the EBIC hyperparameter
test_used: selection of a tuning parameter on an outcome of the analysis
test_indicated: a value fixed a priori, or a sensitivity analysis over gamma reported alongside the results
effect: the detection network sits at the estimator's detection boundary by construction: 907/1000 80% subsamples and 322/400 label-permutation draws of comparable size return an empty graph; the choice is fully disclosed

claim: The lasso GGM 'resulted in a sparse graph with credibly non-zero partial correlations'
design: L1-penalised inverse covariance estimation
test_used: EBIC model selection
test_indicated: no error-controlled statement is available from lasso selection alone
effect: 190 edge parameters are selected per network from 116 and 54 observations with no false-positive control; 'credibly' imports a guarantee the estimator does not provide
